brand_names: Advil PM (note: some brands pair diphenhydramine with ibuprofen, not acetaminophen)
what_its_for: This combination medicine is used to relieve minor aches and pains (such as headache, backache, or muscle pain) AND help you fall asleep. Acetaminophen is the pain reliever, and diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that causes drowsiness to help you sleep. It is meant for short-term use only — typically no more than 2 weeks.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth with a full glass of water. Take it only at bedtime, right before you plan to go to sleep, because it will make you very drowsy. Do not take it if you need to be awake and alert in the next 7 to 8 hours. Take only the dose listed on the label or as directed by your doctor. Do not crush or chew extended-release tablets — swallow them whole.
dosing: For most adults and children 12 years and older: the usual dose is 2 tablets or capsules (acetaminophen 500 mg / diphenhydramine 25 mg each) at bedtime. Do NOT take more than 2 tablets in one night. Do NOT use more than one product at a time that contains acetaminophen, as too much acetaminophen can seriously harm your liver. Do not use for more than 2 weeks in a row without talking to your doctor.
missed_dose: Since this medicine is taken only at bedtime as needed, a 'missed dose' is usually not a concern. Simply take it the next night when you need it. Never double up or take two doses at once to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do NOT store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — check with your pharmacy for a local drug take-back program.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT drink alcohol while taking this medicine — alcohol increases the risk of liver damage from acetaminophen and makes the drowsiness from diphenhydramine much worse. Avoid driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert for at least 7 to 8 hours after taking this medicine. Do not take other medicines that contain acetaminophen (such as NyQuil, Dayquil, Percocet, or other cold and pain medicines) at the same time — this can cause accidental overdose. Avoid other sleep aids, anxiety medicines, muscle relaxers, or prescription pain medicines unless your doctor approves. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or seek immediate medical help if you notice: signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, severe stomach pain, or extreme tiredness; an allergic reaction such as hives, swelling of the face or throat, or trouble breathing; you have taken too much acetaminophen (overdose) — call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222 right away; sleep problems do not improve after 2 weeks; you experience confusion, difficulty urinating, rapid heartbeat, or severe dizziness. Also call your doctor before using this product if you have liver disease, kidney disease, glaucoma, an enlarged prostate, breathing problems (such as asthma or COPD), or if you are pregnant or breastfeeding.
when_it_works: Diphenhydramine usually starts causing drowsiness within 30 minutes, so most people feel sleepy about 30 minutes after taking this medicine. The pain-relieving effect of acetaminophen also begins within 30 to 60 minutes. This is why you should take it right at bedtime — plan to go to sleep shortly after taking your dose.
special_populations: Older adults (65 and over): Use with extra caution. Diphenhydramine can cause significant confusion, dizziness, and increased fall risk in older adults. Talk to your doctor before using this product if you are over 65. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do not use without first speaking to your doctor or pharmacist. Children under 12: This product is NOT recommended for children under 12 years of age. Liver or kidney disease: Use with great caution or avoid entirely — talk to your doctor first. People who drink 3 or more alcoholic drinks per day: Do not use acetaminophen-containing products without medical guidance due to serious liver damage risk.
